sections.history: Thiruvelukkai is one of the 108 Divya Desams and one of the fourteen in Kanchipuram, in Thondai Nadu. Its name is read as Vel-irukkai, 'the dwelling of desire': tradition holds that the Lord came to stay here of his own wish. He is worshipped as Azhagiya Singar, 'the beautiful lion', a gentle form of Narasimha, and also as Mukunda Nayakan, the name under which the master list of Divya Desams often records him. The shrine was sung by Pey Alvar and by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Worship follows the Vaikhanasa agama in the Thenkalai tradition. A modest temple today, it stands close to the Ashtabhuja Perumal temple, and the two are often visited together.
sections.architecture: A small Dravidian temple with a walled court around the sanctum of Azhagiya Singar, shown seated, and a separate shrine for the Goddess Amruthavalli. The vimana over the sanctum is called the Kanaka Vimana, the golden tower, and the temple tank shares the name: Kanaka Saras. The quiet scale of the shrine suits the gentle aspect of its Lord.
sections.legends: This shrine too belongs to the Kanchi cycle of Brahma's sacrifice. When Saraswati sent a fearsome Kapalika to destroy the rite, Vishnu took the form of Narasimha and overcame him — and, the legend continues, remained here as Azhagiya Singar because he loved the place. Another tradition tells that the Lord was first worshipped standing as Mukunda Nayakan and later took his seated form when he appeared to the sage Bhrigu.
sections.festivals: The temple's annual festival falls in Margazhi (December–January), the month that also brings Vaikunta Ekadashi. Narasimha Jayanthi, sacred to every shrine of Narasimha, and the birth-stars of Pey Alvar and Thirumangai Alvar are kept with devotion. Confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: A quiet, unhurried shrine where a pilgrim can stand alone before Azhagiya Singar — a Narasimha of grace rather than fury. Combine it with the nearby Ashtabhuja Perumal temple, and remember that a modest temple's upkeep depends on visitors who come and pray.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; hours can be short at smaller shrines. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: It lies within Kanchipuram town, near the Ashtabhuja Perumal temple; Kanchipuram has a railway station and is reached by road from Chennai (around 70 km), which has the nearest major airport.
